posts.cooked:
This is odd, I'm uncertain what to say. Aside from the reveal to the characters 'in world' of the Infinity Stones this movie just felt... unexciting? It was missing something that the first one had, I didn't get the feeling of heart I got from the first one... and at it's core it seemed largely a retelling of that story, done worse.

 

Stark's lines didn't have the same pop they have had in the past, the team tears itself apart structure was unfulfilling because you knew they would be back stronger than ever, and the death was... predictable and a waste at the same time. With so many people saying "We might not make it out" it was almost pedestrian when it finally did happen, and to make it Quicksilver who had so little screen time (insert joke about his super power) rather than a main character was a cop out. I almost wish it had been Banner instead of the fly-off-into-the-sunset ending they had given him. At the same time it is Whedon's "thing" (to kill someone) so giving me the unexpected by not killing someone would have been different, and they could have made a joke about it afterwards.

 

I didn't see Winter Soldier so I'm only picking things up from the reviews, clips etc that I have seen but doesn't Cap think that Fury is dead? And there was no reaction from anyone on this? If there isn't a deleted scene on this I will be very disappointed.

 

While I have been negative here I do feel that there were good points, Vision coming to the team (and the reason they were so willing to follow), Hawkeye getting some actual character, the Scarlet Witch's visions (I think they spoke to very real fears/desires in all of us, fear of failure or of wanting to belong), not disgarding the last movie building on the plot of what has gone before and Ultron's ultimate end (a son confronting his father in the forest, both unwilling to forgive the generation before).

 

I think I give this movie a stamp of go see it if you liked the others but don't go in expecting too much.

 

And yes, my post in the "nothing" thread was the quote from Thanos.

posts.cooked:
I thought it was great. The jokes were fresh, the action was great and I got a sense of suspense despite knowing none of the big characters were going anywhere. You actually see people die in this one, that didn't happen on screen in the last one.

I loved the focus on Hawkeye. In the comics he is an everyman, a character who has seen it all but isn't extraordinary. A couple years ago he was rated the second best avenger by Marvel , and I think this movie showed part of why that is.

The vision was cool. He wasn't my favorite character but he had a really cool set of motifs. My friends and I were talking about how Ultron wants to be Pinocchio, cutting all his ties and becoming a true living being. Vision on the other hand has a really cool Frankenstein's monster persona. He is created and hated by his father, and ends up killing him. He is even brought to life by a bolt of lightning.  

I loved all the Easter eggs. Every time I sawone, one of my friends would punch me in the shoulder but it was great to see threads reaching out for other parts of the universe.

I am positively ecstatic for Civil War. The new avengers are going to break in half. It's interesting to think about, on one hand you have cap who probably has more bodies, with falcon, widow, Hawkeye, and scarlet witch, but on iron man's side you have arguably stronger heroes with war machine and the vision. It should be interesting to see how it all works out with the panther and the spider as well.

Overall, it was probably a weaker movie than the first, but I think it will stand up a little better than the first, so that's a plus.

posts.cooked:
Ya, I was entertained, but I also got caught up in what I felt were tons of plot holes...for instance, how are the Avengers even together at all? Iron Man destroyed his suits in his movie, Cap lost in shield in his, etc. I thought the silly, unexplained Pool of Asgardian Visions was a nuisance (hopefully it's played out a bit more in the proposed extended cut), and it was annoyingly convenient that the completely disbanded and bankrupt SHIELD was still able to provide a completely operational helicarrier (with staff) at the eleventh hour...

But my biggest qualm with the film was that it simply did not seem that it had a large enough scale. Why does a robotic enemy who can transfer himself through the internet and manipulate everything electronic focus solely on a small, rural city in the middle of nowhere? Why is he not destroying everyones credit and crashing stock markets? Why is he not manipulating literally every robotics manufacturing plant on the globe to accomplish his task? Cap took on an entire global secret agency in his movie...why do we need EVERY Avenger to go punch robots? 

Like I said, I was entertained...but I didn't feel like it was very well written.

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
A quick "I have heard of a place that does X,Y and Z. Lets go there for help" would have been really helpfull. It's ok to have weird places in the world. It's incrediblly jarring however when you are just thrown into one thats so out of place sans any sort of rational or explaination. And why have the professor there in any capacity? It's sloppy and it pulled me out of the movie when those scenes happened.

My other small gripe was that I don't feel Ultron was a really memorable villain, nor did he pose much of a threat himself (yes I get his master plan was a big threat) but I was hoping Stark would build something that could be strong enough to save the world, strong enough to replace the entire Avengers team. That never really happened though as he was easily beat on when the team got their hands on him. Also, I thought it was weird that he managed to obtain his "final form" even before he stole the Vibranium. He went from his "just born" version to the very next scene being in his final state. It would have been nice to see a building or a growth in that character, especially since it's whole central theme was "evolution". 

 

With that being said, I still enjoyed the movie. It was a fun popcorn flick. But it was really sloppy in some respects and that really holds the movie back from being in the same level of film as Winter Soldier, Guardians, or even Avengers 1.

Ant-Man looks solid though. Excited to see that.

I count 5 iterations of Ultron in the movie really:

  • AI only, no body
  • Rag tag "just born" body at the party
  • Intermediate body, used for much of the film
  • Intended ultimate body, became The Vision instead
  • Final body, first introduced with Black Widow, noticed by Iron Man ("have you been juicing?")
You could also count the very last one perhaps (the mostly-destroyed minion body), as a regression.

When it happened, I really wasn't exceptionally surprised. (I mean, I was surprised, but it made sense to me.  ) Speedster characters in a universe like this are just too powerful (and hard!) to accurately portray. The ability to move faster than other people can even think and resolve situations (as Piotr does in Tony's lab) is hard to deal with, and writing them accurately is even harder. There are so many situations in which a speedster should see what's happening and respond long before anyone else even realizes what's happening. 

Anyway, yeah, actually writing speedsters in a realistic way is hard, so keeping him around in the MCU is probably not a good idea.

There are so many situations in which a speedster should see what's happening and respond long before anyone else even realizes what's happening.

Anyway, yeah, actually writing speedsters in a realistic way is hard, so keeping him around in the MCU is probably not a good idea.

My thoughts exactly, Russ. Nailed it.

I thought AOU handled Quicksilver better than Days of Future Past. In DOFP, they resolved the too powerful issue by just not bringing him which made no sense. Leaving him behind just felt contrived. They did a good job with building up to his death with the earlier scene in which he got shot, and so being shot to death didn't feel out of place.
